signatures.name: above_chance_discovery
signatures.description: Successful combinations occur at a rate above 0.55. The original 0.30 threshold underestimated random play in this v1 implementation: the four base elements participate in many recipes and the inventory grows quickly, so a uniform-random combiner with growing inventory empirically reaches ~0.65-0.70 success. Brändle et al. report 0.40-0.50 success rates for adult humans, but human play is *more selective* than random; the threshold here gates whether the agent reproduces success on a per-attempt basis above the empirical chance ceiling.

signatures.name: non_redundant_attempts
signatures.description: Humans avoid retrying the same combination — most attempts use an (element_a_idx, element_b_idx) pair not yet attempted. Operationalized as the proportion of attempts whose ordered pair has not been seen earlier in the session (`is_unique_pair` is computed by the scorer from the (a_idx, b_idx) sequence, treating (a,b) and (b,a) as the same pair). Random play with a small inventory will repeat pairs frequently; a strategic agent keeps this proportion high. Threshold 0.85: a uniform-random combiner over the v1 trial budget repeats enough pairs that the unique-pair rate sits below this.
